body.statement:
Let \(\nu_G=\sqrt{8/3}\), suppose \(C_{\mathrm{env}}\geq \nu_G\), and put \(b=C_{\mathrm{env}}/16\).  Set \(N=3n\), and suppose
\[
 \max\{\|\widehat g\|_\infty,\|\widehat q\|_\infty\}\leq b.
\]
Let \(\mathfrak J_n\) be the uncertainty class in \(\textup{lem:jms-gaussian-fuzzy-benchmark}\) instantiated at sample size \(N\), treatment-noise standard deviation one, power \(s=8\), with each of the fixed bounds on \(|\theta_0|\), \(|g_0(X)|\), and \(|Y|\) equal to \(b\), supplied center \((\widehat g,\widehat q)\), and nuisance radii \((\varepsilon_{g,n},\varepsilon_{q,n})\).  Thus its base laws are the source partially linear laws satisfying \(\eta\mid X\sim\mathcal N(0,1)\) and those three bounds, and its uncertainty restriction is exactly
\[
 \|\widehat g-g_0\|_{L^8(P_X)}\leq\varepsilon_{g,n},
 \qquad
 \|\widehat q-q_0\|_{L^8(P_X)}\leq\varepsilon_{q,n}.
\]
Then
\[
 \mathfrak J_n\subseteq
 \{P\in\mathcal G_n:(\widehat g,\widehat q)\in\mathcal H_n(P)\}.
\]
body.proof_tex:
Fix \(P\in\mathfrak J_n\).  By the definition of the JMS base class recorded in \(\textup{lem:jms-gaussian-fuzzy-benchmark}\), its variables satisfy the partially linear equations
\[
 Y=\theta_0T+f_0(X)+\xi,
 \qquad
 T=g_0(X)+\eta,
\]
with \(E_P[\xi\mid X,T]=0\), and the conditional law of \(\eta\) given \(X\) is \(\mathcal N(0,1)\).  These give \(\textup{ass:outcome-equation}\), \(\textup{ass:treatment-equation}\), and \(\textup{ass:outcome-orthogonality}\).

The conditional Gaussian law is constant in \(X\).  Thus, for Borel sets \(A\subseteq\mathbb R\) and measurable sets \(B\subseteq\mathcal X\),
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 P\{\eta\in A,X\in B\}
 &=E_P\!\left[\mathbf 1_{\{X\in B\}}
      P\{\eta\in A\mid X\}\right] \\
 &=\Phi(A)P_X(B),
 \end{aligned}
\]
where \(\Phi\) is the standard normal law.  Hence \(\eta\perp X\), proving \(\textup{ass:independent-treatment-noise}\), and Gaussian integration gives \(E_P[\eta^2]=1\), proving \(\textup{ass:unit-treatment-variance}\).

It remains to verify the envelope.  The source bounds imply
\[
 |\theta_0|\leq b,
 \qquad |g_0(X)|\leq b,
 \qquad |Y|\leq b
 \quad\text{almost surely}.
\]
Because \(q_0(X)=E_P[Y\mid X]\), conditional Jensen gives \(|q_0(X)|\leq b\) almost surely.  Iterated conditional expectation and the two partially linear equations give
\[
 q_0(X)=\theta_0g_0(X)+f_0(X),
 \qquad
 \xi=Y-q_0(X)-\theta_0\eta.
\]
Consequently,
\[
 |\xi|\leq 2b+b|\eta|,
 \qquad
 \frac{\xi^2}{C_{\mathrm{env}}^2}
 \leq \frac1{32}+\frac{\eta^2}{128}.
\]
For a standard normal variable, direct integration yields
\[
 E_P\exp(\eta^2/c^2)=(1-2/c^2)^{-1/2}
 \quad(c^2>2).
\]
In particular, the defining Luxemburg inequality for the sub-Gaussian norm is an equality at \(c^2=8/3\), so \(\|\eta\|_{\psi_2}=\nu_G\leq C_{\mathrm{env}}\).  The preceding pointwise inequality also gives
\[
 E_P\exp\!\left(\frac{\xi^2}{C_{\mathrm{env}}^2}\right)
 \leq e^{1/32}(1-1/64)^{-1/2}<2.
\]
For completeness, the last strict inequality follows after taking logarithms from \(-\log(1-x)\leq2x\) at \(x=1/64\), because the logarithm of the left side is at most \(3/64<\log 2\).  Therefore \(\|\xi\|_{\psi_2}\leq C_{\mathrm{env}}\).  Since \(b<C_{\mathrm{env}}\), all components of \(\textup{ass:uniform-envelope}\) hold.  By \(\textup{def:jms-law-class}\), \(P\in\mathcal P_n\); the marginal law \(\eta\sim\mathcal N(0,1)\) and \(\textup{def:gaussian-branch}\) then give \(P\in\mathcal G_n\).

Finally, the \(s=8\) uncertainty restriction defining \(\mathfrak J_n\) is
\[
 \|\widehat g-g_0\|_{L^8(P_X)}\leq\varepsilon_{g,n},
 \qquad
 \|\widehat q-q_0\|_{L^8(P_X)}\leq\varepsilon_{q,n}.
\]
These are exactly the two inequalities in \(\textup{def:supplied-fit-set}\), so \((\widehat g,\widehat q)\in\mathcal H_n(P)\).  Both asserted memberships follow.
